text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Three feared dead in air force plane crash in the north.

- Central bank says three distressed banks under its administration -- African Continental Bank, New Nigeria Bank and National Bank of Nigeria -- have been sold to "fit and proper" investors and should resume business soon.
- Salary increase at Dunlop Nigeria Plc boomerangs as 1,000 workers say it is not enough, riot, are shut out and factory is closed.
- Delay in payment of two months salary to staff of department of petroleum resources which oversees crude oil exports puts the workers on collision course with management.
- U.N. official says planned visit of two U.N. rapporteurs to Nigeria to investigate human rights shelved after failure to agree with the military government on itinerary of the team.
- Not less than 10 companies have submitted bids to the federal government for 183 "marginal" or small oil fields that government wants tapped.
- Wireless Telecoms Limited, licensed by the authorities to run a private communication network, is offering five million shares by way of private placement to raise 50 million naira.
- Michael Ajasin, ailing 88-year-old national chairman of the umbrella opposition group NADECO, is in stable condition in hospital, his doctor says.
- Task force investigating spate of bomb blasts in Nigeria recommends that former finance minister Olu Falae, detained since December, should be tried, police sources say.
- Liquidity in banking system pushes lending rates down to 10 percent from 13 percent a fortnight ago.
- Chevron Corp's Nigerian unit allocates 400 million naira this year for spending on community development projects in oil-producing areas.
